title: 地心游记
author: Jules Verne（WordVerse 改写版）
one_line: 跟着羊皮纸向下走，穿过地下的海回到阳光里。

sentences.en: In May 1863 Professor Lidenbrock of Hamburg came home from the old bookshops carrying a battered Icelandic manuscript, talking to it under his breath as if the book were a colleague; he taught geology, the science that reads fire and stone beneath our feet, and he attacked difficult books the way other men eat dinner — quickly, noisily, and without any fear of indigestion.
sentences.zh: 1863年5月，汉堡的黎登布洛克教授从旧书店回来，怀里抱着一本虫蛀的冰岛文古书，嘴里对它念念有词，仿佛那书是他的同行；他教的是地质学，一门读我们脚下火与石头的学问，而啃难书这件事，他做起来像别人吃晚饭——又快、又响、毫不怕消化不良。

sentences.en: His house in the Königstrasse, half wood and half brick, leaned a little like its neighbours, and Martha the cook trembled whenever the professor returned early; on this Sunday he came early, and the whole household understood that dinner would have to wait for whatever had entered the door inside that bundle of old paper — dinner which, on this particular Sunday, finally arrived at midnight, cold and apologetic.
sentences.zh: 他家的房子半木半砖，和邻居一样微微歪着；厨娘玛尔莎一见教授提前回家就发怵。这个星期天他偏偏提前回来了，全家都明白：晚饭得给那卷从门里进来的旧纸让路——而这顿晚饭在这个星期天，最后是半夜才端上来的，凉的，还带着歉意。

sentences.en: Out of the cover fell a parchment of runic letters, which submitted to no ordinary reading; the professor's nephew Axel, a young man of nineteen who loved Gräuben and hated adventures, tried every key his uncle could think of, until the uncle, in a fury, transferred the whole problem to him with the complaint that geology was patient and nephews were not.
sentences.zh: 书皮里掉出一页写满如尼字母的羊皮纸，怎么念都不成句；教授的侄子阿克塞尔，一个爱着格劳本、讨厌冒险的十九岁青年，把伯父想得出的各种读法试了个遍；最后伯父发着火把整个难题转手甩给他，抱怨说：地质学有的是耐心，侄子可没有。

sentences.en: Axel counted the letters and treated the page as a problem of geometry; then, reading the runic letters backwards, so that Latin words stood out of them, he brought a voice across three hundred years, and the discovery, instead of pleasing him, filled him with a cold private grief.
sentences.zh: 阿克塞尔数着字母，把这页纸当成一道几何题来解；随后倒着去念那些如尼字母，拉丁文的词句便从字母里立了出来，一个声音穿过三百年走到了他面前；而这个发现没有让他高兴，反倒让他心里一凉，独自难过起来。

sentences.en: "Descend, bold traveller, and you will reach the centre of the terrestrial globe," said the parchment, and beneath the Latin stood the name of Arne Saknussemm, an Icelandic scholar of the sixteenth century, who had written his secret and then hidden it, as men do, in the one place everybody can read and nobody thinks to look: a cipher inside an old book.
sentences.zh: "下来吧，勇敢的旅行者，你将抵达地心。"羊皮纸上这样写，拉丁文下面落着一个名字：阿尔奈·萨克努姗，十六世纪的冰岛学者；他写下自己的秘密，又照人的老习惯把它藏进了一个人人都读得到、却谁也想不起去看的地方——一本旧书里的密码。

sentences.en: The transmitted route was plain enough: the crater of Sneffels in Iceland, and the passage marked by the shadow of the crater's rim in the last days of June, when the north-west sun points the way down into the earth's own territory.
sentences.zh: 传递下来的路线写得够明白：冰岛的斯奈菲尔火山口，以及六月的最后几天里，火山口边缘的山影所指的那条通道——那时，偏西北的太阳会指明通往大地自己领地的下行之路。

sentences.en: Axel, who had learned his geology obediently, objected that the heat of the deep would bake them like bread; the thermometer, he said, rises so many degrees for every so many feet of descent, and the centre of the earth must be a furnace that no instrument and no traveller could support — the centre, in his obedient view, was a settled question, and the answer was no.
sentences.zh: 阿克塞尔规规矩矩学过地质学，他反对说：深处的热会把人像面包一样烤熟；他说，温度计每下降多少英尺就升高多少度，地心必定是一座炉子，任何仪器、任何旅人都招架不住——在他这个听话学生看来，地心是个早有定论的问题，答案是：去不得。

sentences.en: His uncle asked, with terrible calm, which thermometer had ever been carried low enough to prove it; a science, he declared, that never goes down is a science built on the rungs above the cellar, and Iceland's geothermal springs were exactly the door to that cellar.
sentences.zh: 伯父以一种吓人的平静反问：哪一支温度计曾经被带到那么深、证明过这一点？他宣称：一门从不下行的科学，是只建在地窖以上那几级梯子上的科学；而冰岛的地热泉，正是通向那个地窖的门。

sentences.en: "The terrain up there," said he, unfolding a map, "is lava and ice side by side, the strangest mixture on the surface of this terrestrial ball; Saknussemm saw it and went down anyway, and if a sixteenth-century scholar with a rope and a lamp could do it, the nineteenth century cannot very well stay home."
sentences.zh: "那上面的地貌，"他摊开一张地图说，"是熔岩和冰雪并肩而立，这颗陆地球体表面最古怪的混合；萨克努姗见识过了，照样下去了——如果十六世纪的学者靠一根绳、一盏灯都做得到，十九世纪总不好赖在家里吧。"

sentences.en: "Science is built of descending steps," the professor declared; "every instrument we carry down brings one fact up from the dark, and a geologist who does not go down is like an astronomer who never lifts his head; the facts of the deep have been sitting under the feet of scholars for centuries, too far beneath their dignity to be fetched."
sentences.zh: "科学是由向下的台阶砌成的，"教授宣称，"我们带下去的每件仪器，都能从黑暗里带上一个事实上来；不肯往下走的地质学家，就像从不抬头的天文学家；深处的那些事实，几百年来就一直待在学者们的脚底下，只是离他们的体面太远，没人肯弯腰去捡。"

sentences.en: In the days that followed, ropes, tools, instruments, guns and a medicine chest were collected, and the little expedition constructed itself in a corner of the study like a living thing; Axel watched the pile grow the way a condemned man watches a scaffold being built.
sentences.zh: 接下来那些天，绳子、工具、仪器、枪支和药箱一件件收拢来，这支小小的远征队在书房一角渐渐成形，像个活物；阿克塞尔看着那堆东西越长越高，像死囚看着给自己搭绞架。

sentences.en: Axel submitted at last, the way the fearful always submit to the confident, and he wrote a sad farewell to Gräuben, his gentle bride-to-be, in which he tried very hard to make a lifetime's unhappiness sound like a short scientific inconvenience.
sentences.zh: 阿克塞尔终究还是屈服了——胆小的人总归拗不过自信的人；他给温柔的未婚妻格劳本写下一封伤感的告别信，信里他竭尽全力，想把一辈子的不幸说成一场短暂的科学上的不便。

sentences.en: Gräuben herself, calmer than either of them, answered that a man who came back from the centre of the earth would come back worth having, and this small sentence travelled with Axel like an extra compass; two days later they were rolling north by rail and steamer, through Denmark, towards the volcanic island where the earth breathes through every crack.
sentences.zh: 格劳本本人倒比他们两个都镇定，回信说：从地心回来的人，回来时必定更值得拥有；这句话不长，却像一件备用的罗盘，一路跟着阿克塞尔。两天后，他们已乘着火车和轮船一路向北，穿过丹麦，驶向那座大地处处从裂缝里呼吸的火山之岛。

sentences.en: The parchment slept in the professor's pocket, the thermometer and the barometer slept in their cases, and the terrible Latin sentence slept inside Axel's head, where it woke him at three in the morning: descend, bold traveller, and you will reach the centre of the terrestrial globe.
sentences.zh: 羊皮纸在教授口袋里安睡，温度计和气压计在各自的箱子里安睡，那句可怕的拉丁文却睡在阿克塞尔的脑袋里，凌晨三点还把他叫醒：下来吧，勇敢的旅行者，你将抵达地心。

questions.q: What did the Latin message on the parchment tell the bold traveller to do?
options: Sail west across the ocean to a new continent.
Descend and reach the centre of the terrestrial globe.
Climb the highest peak of Iceland.
Translate more runic manuscripts in Copenhagen.
questions.explain: 第5句羊皮纸上写 "Descend, bold traveller, and you will reach the centre of the terrestrial globe"，落款是十六世纪冰岛学者萨克努姗。

questions.q: How did Axel finally succeed in reading the runic cipher?
options: By holding the parchment in front of a fire.
By asking a professor of geology in Denmark.
By counting the letters and then reading them backwards, as a problem of geometry.
By copying the letters into Gräuben's letter.
questions.explain: 第4句 "Axel counted the letters and treated the page as a problem of geometry; then, reading the runic letters backwards... he brought a voice across three hundred years"——数字母、倒着读，密码才解开。

questions.q: How did the professor answer Axel's fear that the heat of the deep would bake them?
options: He promised they would turn back at the first sign of warmth.
He asked which thermometer had ever been carried low enough to prove it.
He agreed to take a shorter journey first.
He said a frozen sea awaited them below Iceland.
questions.explain: 第8句教授以吓人的平静反问 "which thermometer had ever been carried low enough to prove it"，并把从不下行的科学比作只建在地窖以上几级梯子上的科学。

questions.q: Gräuben's reply is said to travel with Axel "like an extra compass". What does this suggest?
options: She gave him a real compass as a parting gift.
Her faith steadies him and gives his journey a direction, as a compass gives a ship.
She will follow them secretly to Iceland.
Her words warn him that he is going the wrong way.
questions.explain: 第13句她回信说"从地心回来的人，回来时必定更值得拥有"——一个罗盘不改变船，只给船一个方向；她的信任在整趟旅途中为胆小的阿克塞尔充当了精神上的罗盘。

questions.q: The word "geothermal" is built from two roots, one meaning earth and one meaning heat. What are Iceland's geothermal springs?
options: Springs heated by fire from inside the earth.
Springs that freeze in summer and melt in winter.
Springs used by geologists for drinking water.
Springs that appear only at the equator.
questions.explain: 第8句 "Iceland's geothermal springs were exactly the door to that cellar"——geothermal（geo 大地 + therm 热）指由地下之火烧热的泉水，正是通往"地窖"的门。

sentences.en: Iceland received them with grey moss, black lava fields and steam rising from geothermal springs — a country where the earth breathes through every crack — and the professor, standing in the boat with his nose in the wind, declared that no geologist had ever been welcomed so warmly by his own subject matter, nor ever scolded by it so promptly, as the rain began at once.
sentences.zh: 冰岛用灰苔藓、黑色熔岩原和温泉里升腾的蒸汽迎接了他们——一个大地从每条裂缝里呼吸的国度；教授站在船上，迎着风，宣称从来没有哪个地质学家，被自己这门学科如此热情地欢迎过——也从来没有谁这么快就被这门学科劈头训斥，因为雨说下就下。

sentences.en: In Reykjavik they were received with politeness and quiet astonishment; their host offered them, with great ceremony, the worst soup Axel had ever tasted and the best care a poor country could give, and by lamplight the professor studied his parchment while Axel studied his own growing fear, each with the same gravity, while the lamp between them burned down without prejudice toward either study.
sentences.zh: 在雷克雅未克，人们礼貌又惊讶地接待了他们；主人极其郑重地端上阿克塞尔此生喝过的最差的汤，也倾其所有，拿出了这个穷国能给的最周到的照料；灯下，教授研究羊皮纸，阿克塞尔研究自己越涨越高的恐惧，两个人一样专注，而他们中间那盏灯不偏不倚地烧了下去，对两门学问一视同仁。

sentences.en: Their guide was Hans, a duck hunter of perfect silence, who accepted the wages, transmitted their baggage to his back, and never once smiled; he spoke about three words of Danish a day, used fewer, and would, over the months to come, hold the whole expedition together like an invisible nail.
sentences.zh: 向导叫汉斯，一个猎鸭人，安静到了家；他收下工钱，把行李往背上一背，从头到尾没笑过一次；他丹麦语一天说三个词，实际用到的更少；而在往后的岁月里，他会像一根看不见的钉子，把整支远征队牢牢钉在一起。

sentences.en: The terrain rose as they walked: columns of basalt, plains of ancient lava, ridges where no grass had ever taken territory, and hot brooks that ran, inexplicably, straight out of the ice; Axel, working with the instruments, found that the rocks changed as they climbed, and the professor said the mountain was keeping a diary in stone, and that they were walking up its pages.
sentences.zh: 走着走着，地势节节升高：玄武岩石柱、古老的熔岩平原、寸草从未占领过的山脊，还有一条条说不出道理、径直从冰里冒出来的热溪；阿克塞尔摆弄仪器，发现越往上岩石越不一样；教授说，这座山一直在用石头写日记，而他们正沿着书页往上走。

sentences.en: "You see thermal water running out of a glacier," the professor observed once; "fire and ice holding hands, so to speak; geology is the only science in which the two extremes of the world write each other letters in the same rock, and Iceland is their post office."
sentences.zh: "你们看见温泉水从冰川里流出来了，"教授有一回感叹，"可以说是火和冰手拉手；地质学是唯一一门让世界上两个极端在同一块岩石里互相通信的科学，而冰岛，就是它们的邮局。"

sentences.en: Axel's thermometer served as their honest companion; at every rest he read it, noted the figure, and by evening the three of them knew the temperature of the air, the temperature of the water and the temperature of the professor's enthusiasm, of which only the last never fell.
sentences.zh: 阿克塞尔的温度计是队伍里最诚实的伙伴；每回歇脚他都读一读、记下数字，到晚上，三个人就都知道了空气的温度、水的温度，还有教授热情的温度——三样里头，只有最后一样从不下降。

sentences.en: At the summit of Sneffels three rocky chimneys stood open, like the mouths of wells long out of use; Saknussemm's marks, half eaten by time, pointed to the north-western one, and the professor kissed the scratch as a man kisses a letter from a friend.
sentences.zh: 斯奈菲尔山顶敞着三个岩石烟囱口，像久已废置的井口；萨克努姗刻下的记号已被岁月啃掉一半，正指着北偏西那一个；教授吻了吻那道刻痕，像吻一封老朋友的来信。

sentences.en: On the last day of June the shadow of the crater's rim fell upon that chimney at the very hour the parchment had named; "Into the terrestrial unknown!" cried Lidenbrock, and lowered himself first, his voice coming back up out of the hole, smaller than a boy's; it was, Axel noted, exactly the voice of a man who has just discovered that the earth is larger than his lecture.
sentences.zh: 六月的最后一天，火山口边缘的影子恰好落在那个烟囱口上，正应了羊皮纸写明的时辰；"向着地底的未知！"黎登布洛克喊了一声，第一个下了洞；他的声音从洞里回上来，比小孩子的还细；阿克塞尔听出来了，这正是一个人刚发现大地竟比他的讲课还大时，会有的那种嗓音。

sentences.en: The descent ran down a gallery of lava walls, seventeen hundred feet of it, and the grey daylight above them shrank as they went, first to a window, then to a star, then to a memory; at the bottom they entered a subterranean gallery, one black geological night, where Axel's thermometer read a comfortable ten degrees.
sentences.zh: 下行通道贴着熔岩壁一路向下，足有一千七百英尺；头顶那片灰白的天光随他们的脚步不断缩小，先缩成一扇窗，再缩成一颗星，最后缩成一段记忆；井底是一段地下通道，一场地质学意义上的黑夜，阿克塞尔的温度计读出了宜人的十度。

sentences.en: The professor delivered a lecture on the crust, complete and confident, with his lantern for a lamp, Axel for an audience and Hans for neither; Axel listened, and submitted privately to the pleasure of being afraid, which is a pleasure the young never confess to.
sentences.zh: 教授就地开讲一堂关于地壳的课，讲得完备而笃定：灯笼充当他讲课的灯，阿克塞尔权当听众，汉斯两样都不当；阿克塞尔听着，私下里却屈服于那种害怕的快感——这种快感，年轻人是从来不肯承认的。

sentences.en: Where the rock broke off, Hans constructed a rope ladder with the calm of a man building a fence, and each evening he raised a hut of lava slabs; no money in the surface world, Axel observed, could have hired that amount of peace, nor, for any money, reproduced it.
sentences.zh: 岩壁断开的地方，汉斯就地搭起绳梯，那份镇定像农人在围篱笆；每天傍晚，他垒起一座熔岩板小屋；阿克塞尔看在眼里：地面上的世界出多少钱，也雇不来这一份安之若素——更出多少钱，也仿造不出这一份安之若素。

sentences.en: Halls of granite opened around them, hollowed by some ancient water, walls that met and parted like the pages of an enormous book; the professor read them aloud and named their era as he passed, a tourist in the architecture of the planet; and Axel, walking behind, began at last to feel something like wonder, which he carefully disguised as caution.
sentences.zh: 花岗岩的大厅在四周次第敞开，是远古的水掏空的；岩壁相遇又分开，像一部巨书的书页；教授边走边高声诵读，随口叫出它们的纪元，俨然这座行星建筑里的一名游客；而走在后面的阿克塞尔，心里头一回生出一点近乎惊叹的东西——他小心翼翼，把它伪装成了谨慎。

sentences.en: The deeper they walked, the warmer Axel expected the walls to become, and he said so; his uncle answered that the theory of a fiery centre was exactly the sort of doctrine that grows comfortable sitting in armchairs, and that only a descent could turn doctrine into fact.
sentences.zh: 越往深走，阿克塞尔越觉得岩壁该越来越烫，他说了出来；伯父回答：地心炽热说，正是那种赖在扶手椅里养得舒舒服服的教条——唯有下行，才能把教条变成事实。

sentences.en: That expectation, as the coming days would show, was quite wrong; but for that night the three travellers slept in the hand of the mountain, the professor dreaming of the centre of the earth, Hans of nothing at all, and Axel of Gräuben waving on the quays of Copenhagen.
sentences.zh: 往后的日子会证明，这个预感错得离谱；但那天夜里，三个旅人睡在大山的掌心里：教授梦见地心，汉斯什么也没梦见，阿克塞尔梦见哥本哈根码头上挥手的格劳本。

questions.q: What kind of guide was Hans?
options: A talkative professor of Icelandic.
A silent duck hunter who never once smiled.
A young student of geology from Hamburg.
A fisherman hired in Reykjavik harbour.
questions.explain: 第3句 "a duck hunter of perfect silence... never once smiled"，他一天只说三个丹麦词；第11句又写他搭绳梯垒石屋的那份安之若素。

questions.q: How did the travellers know which of the three chimneys was the way down?
options: Hans chose the widest and driest one.
Axel's thermometer fell in the north-western one.
Saknussemm's marks pointed to it, and the rim's shadow fell on it at the hour the parchment named.
They drew lots among the three and followed the professor.
questions.explain: 第7句萨克努姗的记号指着北偏西那个口，第8句六月最后一天火山口边缘的影子恰好落在那里，正应羊皮纸写明的时辰。

questions.q: What did Axel's thermometer read at the bottom of the descent?
options: A boiling temperature.
A comfortable ten degrees.
Forty degrees below zero.
Nothing — the instrument had broken.
questions.explain: 第9句 "at the bottom they entered a subterranean gallery... where Axel's thermometer read a comfortable ten degrees"，井底温度宜人。

questions.q: Axel "submitted privately to the pleasure of being afraid" during the lecture. What does this suggest about him?
options: He has secretly begun to enjoy the adventure he claimed to dread.
He is planning to escape back to Hamburg alone.
He has fallen asleep and is dreaming of Gräuben.
He is mocking his uncle's science to himself.
questions.explain: 第10句他嘴上反对、心里却"屈服于害怕的快感"，而"这种快感年轻人从来不肯承认"——结合前文他看装备像看绞架、后又热泪告别，可见这个惧怕冒险的青年已开始暗暗享受冒险。

questions.q: In sentence 4, "the terrain rose as they walked" — what does the word "terrain" mean?
options: The temperature of the ground.
The physical character of a stretch of land — its rocks, slopes and surface.
A border between two territories.
The age of the rocks, counted in centuries.
questions.explain: 第4句列举了 terrain 所含之物：玄武岩柱、熔岩平原、山脊、热溪——terrain（词根 terr，土地）指一片土地的自然面貌：岩层、坡度与地表。

sentences.en: After some days the walls grew strange in another way: the thermometer, read at every rest, showed the temperature falling as they went down, and Axel, to whom every number was a comfort, recorded the scandal in his notebook with a hand that was almost steady.
sentences.zh: 过了些天，岩壁又古怪起来：每次歇脚都看温度计，越往下走，温度反而越低；对阿克塞尔来说，每个数字都是一种安慰，他把这件"丑闻"记进本子，那只手几乎称得上稳。

sentences.en: "A thermal scandal!" laughed the professor, delighted; "the old doctrine of inner heat is wrong, and only a geologist who comes down can prove it wrong — which is precisely why we are here, my boy, and not in some armchair in Hamburg."
sentences.zh: "热学丑闻！"教授大笑，乐不可支，"地心发热的旧理论错了，而只有亲自下来的地质学家才证明得了它错——这，孩子，正是我们在这里、而不是坐在汉堡哪把扶手椅里的原因。"

sentences.en: The terrain changed as well: coal, then slate, then a reddish rock that the professor greeted like an old friend and named aloud, and the passage turned, dropped and turned again, like a sentence that keeps changing its grammar, so that a man walking it becomes a grammarian of stone.
sentences.zh: 地层也变了：先是煤，再是板岩，然后是一种微红的岩石，教授见了它像见到老朋友，高声叫出它的名字；通道转了又落，落了又转，像一句不停改换语法的句子——走在里面的人，便被逼成了石头的语法学家。

sentences.en: Rushing water sounded inside the rock; Hans set his ear against the wall, waited, struck a hole with the pick, and a boiling spring burst out; they let it cool in their water bottles, drank, and followed the underground stream like a guide through the deeper galleries of the mountain, down one stair of stone after another, each turning colder, each turning stranger.
sentences.zh: 岩石深处传来奔水的声音；汉斯把耳朵贴上岩壁，等了等，几镐头凿开一个口，一股滚烫的泉水喷涌而出；他们接在水壶里等它凉，喝了，随后让这条地下溪流当向导，领他们穿过大山更深的走廊——一级石阶接着一级石阶地往下去，每转一弯，更冷一分，也更古怪一分。

sentences.en: Axel feared the water at first, having read of hypothermia and of travellers dead of cold in wet caverns, though the danger here, as it turned out, was exactly the opposite; the stream stayed warm as a bath, and his fear, finding nothing to hold, attached itself instead to an enormous shadow that swam past their lamps far ahead.
sentences.zh: 起初阿克塞尔怕这水，因为他读到过失温症，读到过旅人死在阴湿洞穴里的事——虽然这回的危险，恰恰相反；溪水一直温热如浴，他的恐惧找不到抓手，便改去抱住远处从他们灯前游过的那道巨大的影子。

sentences.en: The passage opened upon a shore that Axel refused, at first, to believe in: a subterranean sea, wide and still, faintly lit from within, under a ceiling of rock that served for sky, with a coastline of white sand and a horizon that ended in darkness instead of distance — an arrangement of the world that seemed to have been drawn up without any reference to the sun.
sentences.zh: 通道尽头豁然是一片海岸，阿克塞尔起初拒绝相信：一片地下海，宽阔安静，幽幽自明，头顶的岩石穹顶权当天空；岸线是白沙，海平线的尽头不是远方，而是黑暗——这世界的布局，拟定的时候，似乎压根没跟太阳商量过。

sentences.en: "This is the greatest exhibit in the museum of geology," said the professor, taking off his hat to it; Hans, with no comment, constructed a raft of fossil wood and sailcloth, and on it the three crossed the waters that Saknussemm had crossed before them, three hundred years apart and one single sea.
sentences.zh: "这是地质学博物馆里最大的一件展品。"教授说着，向它脱帽致意；汉斯不发一言，用硅化木和帆布造了只木筏；三人乘着它，渡过萨克努姗当年渡过的同一片水——相隔三百年，同一片海。

sentences.en: Along the banks stood white mushrooms thirty feet tall, trees of an older thermal world, pale as candles; the raft slid beneath them slowly, and Axel tried to imagine the light that had once fed them, and could not: whatever sun had shone on that forest of fungi, it had set before Greece was a village.
sentences.zh: 沿岸立着三十英尺高的巨型白蘑菇，属于一个更古老炎热世界的树木，白得像蜡烛；木筏从它们底下缓缓滑过；阿克塞尔试着想象曾经喂养过它们的光，却想象不出——无论照过这片菌类森林的是哪颗太阳，在希腊还只是个村落之前，它就已经落山了。

sentences.en: The mast was a young fir that some ancient flood had carried down alive, its needles still green, defying geology like a man arriving at a funeral in summer clothes; a wind that should not exist filled the sail, and transmitted them along the dark tide.
sentences.zh: 桅杆是一株被远古洪水活着冲下来的小冷杉，针叶还绿着，对地质学公然不服，像个穿着夏装来奔丧的人；一阵本不该存在的风灌满了帆，载着他们沿黑色潮水前行。

sentences.en: Axel, watching the water, saw the shadow of an enormous swimmer pass beneath the raft — a lizard of the primary ages, the professor said, with a modesty of statement that did not hide his pride; the beast offered neither proof of itself nor any comfort, and went away, and Axel's knuckles were white on the rope.
sentences.zh: 阿克塞尔望着水面，看见一个庞大游泳者的影子从筏下掠过——"原始时代的蜥蜴，"教授说，语气收敛得恰到好处，却掩不住得意；那家伙既不留下证明，也不给人安慰，自顾自去了；阿克塞尔攥着绳子的指节，白得像骨头。

sentences.en: The professor named the sea after himself, a cape after Gräuben, and a bay after the university, and Axel observed that territorial instinct survives every darkness; men, he wrote that evening, are the only animals that carry flags in their hearts, and the flags had come down with them, and planted themselves at the first corner of the dark.
sentences.zh: 教授用自己的名字命名这片海，用格劳本命名一个海角，又用大学命名一处海湾；阿克塞尔看得明白：占地为王的本能熬得过任何黑暗；他当晚写道，人是唯一一种心里揣着旗帜的动物，而如今，旗帜也跟着他们降到了地底，并在黑暗的第一个街角，就把自己插上了。

sentences.en: A storm of the lower world rose in the black afternoon: strange lightning without thunder played upon the water, the sail stood out like a sheet of ice, and the raft fled before the wind like a train, with what felt like the whole electric weight of the sky sitting on its mast.
sentences.zh: 下界起了风暴，在黑沉沉的"午后"：无声的怪异电光在水面游走，帆绷得像一面冰，木筏在风前逃，像一列火车——整片天空的电流，仿佛都坐在它的桅杆上。

sentences.en: One ball of electric fire settled on the mast, ran down the halliards, leapt at Axel's face and passed; when it had passed, the compass read backwards, and nobody noticed, and the expedition, proud of its instruments, sailed confidently on in the wrong direction.
sentences.zh: 一团电火落在桅杆上，顺着升降索溜下来，扑向阿克塞尔的脸，又掠了过去；它过去之后，罗盘的指针倒了过来，却没有一个人发觉；这支以仪器自傲的远征队，满怀信心地朝错误的方向继续航行。

sentences.en: "We are circling," the professor admitted at last, tapping the shore that should not have been there; the sea had brought them back, and it was Axel, thermometer of fear and of measurement both, who understood first that they were lost — lost in a world that no map on the surface of the earth had ever been asked to describe.
sentences.zh: "我们在兜圈子。"教授终于承认，手杖敲着那片本不该出现的海岸；是这片海把他们送了回来；而头一个明白他们已经迷路的，是阿克塞尔——他既是恐惧的温度计，也是测量用的温度计——迷在了这样一个世界里：地面上任何一张地图，都不曾被要求描绘过它。

questions.q: What "thermal scandal" did the thermometer reveal as they went down?
options: The temperature rose exactly as the old theory predicted.
The temperature was falling the deeper they went.
The thermometer had stopped working in the damp.
The temperature changed with the hour of the day.
questions.explain: 第1句 "the thermometer, read at every rest, showed the temperature falling as they went down"，第2句教授大笑称之为 "a thermal scandal"，并说这恰恰证明了地心发热的旧教条错了。

questions.q: What did the deeper passage finally open upon?
options: A dead end of solid granite.
A subterranean sea under a ceiling of rock, lit faintly from within.
A city left by ancient travellers.
A frozen cavern of blue ice.
questions.explain: 第6句 "a subterranean sea, wide and still, faintly lit from within, under a ceiling of rock that served for sky"——通道尽头是一片以岩石为天空、幽幽自明的地下海。

questions.q: What stood along the banks of the underground sea?
options: Olive trees and tall grass.
White mushrooms thirty feet tall, pale as candles.
Reeds and ordinary ferns.
Apple trees heavy with fruit.
questions.explain: 第8句 "white mushrooms thirty feet tall, trees of an older thermal world, pale as candles"，岸边立着三十英尺高的巨型白蘑菇。

questions.q: After the storm, the compass read backwards and nobody noticed. What does this episode suggest?
options: The travellers' confidence in their instruments blinds them in a world with different rules.
Hans has deliberately turned the compass around.
The professor's calculations were always wrong.
Compasses cannot work north of the Arctic Circle.
questions.explain: 第13句罗盘倒转"却无人发觉"，队伍"以仪器自傲……满怀信心地朝错误的方向航行"，第14句他们绕了一圈回到原地——在地下世界里，他们最信赖的仪器恰恰背叛了他们。

questions.q: Axel had read of travellers dying of "hypothermia" in wet caverns. What does the word mean?
options: A dangerous loss of the body's heat.
A disease caught from bad water.
A fear of closed places.
A wound caused by falling rock.
questions.explain: 第5句 "having read of hypothermia and of travellers dead of cold in wet caverns"——hypo（低）+ therm（热）+ ia，指体温降到危险水平的失温症；本句说这里的危险"恰恰相反"，因为水其实温热如浴。

sentences.en: The new shore ended against a wall of granite that ran out into the sea; there was no passage, and Saknussemm's marks went no further than a blunt arrow scratched at the height of a man's heart, like a signature left on a locked door, pointing at nothing but the past.
sentences.zh: 新海岸的尽头顶着一面花岗岩壁，一路插进海里；没有通道，萨克努姗的记号到这儿也断了，只剩一道齐着人心口高的钝箭头，像留在上锁门板上的一枚签名——指着哪儿都不指，只指着过去。

sentences.en: In the ash Axel found a rusted dagger, its blade thinned by three centuries; Saknussemm himself had stood here, stopped by the same stone, and had either left the weapon in proof or lost it in despair — the past, for once, signing a witness statement.
sentences.zh: 灰烬里，阿克塞尔捡到一柄锈蚀的小刀，刀刃被三个世纪磨薄了；三百年前，萨克努姗就站在这里，被同一块石头挡住；这柄武器，或是他留下的凭据，或是他绝望中失落的——过去这一回，破天荒签了一份证人证词。

sentences.en: Refusing defeat, the professor constructed a mine of gunpowder and set the charge in the one crack the wall had offered, with Hans holding the raft and Axel holding the last sane objection; the blast opened the granite, and the sea poured in upon them, raft and all, with a fury nobody had budgeted for.
sentences.zh: 教授不肯认输，布置了一处火药爆破，把药包塞进岩壁仅有的那道裂缝里；汉斯死死按住木筏，阿克塞尔攥着最后一个还算清醒的反对意见；炸药轰开花岗岩，海水裹着木筏连人带行李一起灌进裂口，那股狂怒，没有任何人的预算里算到过。

sentences.en: Down a boiling shaft they were carried, turned, pressed and spun like laundry; and then, in the deepest dark, the water began to grow hotter about them, and the raft began to feel less like a boat than like a pot on a fire, and every knot in the wood of the raft was beginning to smell like soup.
sentences.zh: 他们被带下一条滚烫的竖井，被翻转、挤压、甩荡，像一锅待洗的衣物；随后，在最深的黑暗里，四周的水开始越来越热，木筏渐渐不像一条船，倒像坐在火上的一口锅，连筏身上每一个木头节子，都开始散出汤的香味。

sentences.en: The thermometer climbed past every number Axel dared to read aloud, and the walls grew bright in a way walls should not; "not the centre of the earth," the professor shouted over the roar, "but a channel of it — a geyser pipe, a geothermal lift, and it is going up!"
sentences.zh: 温度计一路爬升，数字高得阿克塞尔不敢念出声，岩壁发起一种岩壁不该有的亮；"这不是地心，"教授顶着轰鸣大喊，"是地心的一条通道——一条间歇泉的管子，一部地热电梯，而它正在上行！"

sentences.en: Steam lifted them from below: the old volcanic pipe had become a lift driven by geothermal fire, rising for the first time in ten thousand years; Axel held his uncle's hand, Hans held the mast, and the earth did the rest, throwing them out of a crater into the warm sea of the Mediterranean.
sentences.zh: 蒸汽从下方把他们托起：那条古老的火山管道变成了一部地热之火驱动的电梯，一万年来头一回向上开动；阿克塞尔攥着伯父的手，汉斯抱住桅杆，剩下的事交给大地——它把他们从火山口抛进了地中海温暖的海水。

sentences.en: They were tossed out under the open sky at the foot of a smoking rock; the shore, when their eyes could bear the light again, was Stromboli, an island off the sunny coast of Italy, and their volcano had thrown them, as the professor computed within the week, across half the hemisphere — a result which no geologist would have dared to put on paper.
sentences.zh: 他们被抛出火山口，落在青天底下一块冒烟的岩石脚下；等眼睛受得住光亮再看，那片海岸是斯特龙博利岛，地中海里的一座岛，就在意大利阳光明媚的近海；教授不出一周便算出来：他们那座火山，把他们抛过了半个地球——这个结果，哪个地质学家也不敢写进论文。

sentences.en: Fishermen fed them bread and wine and refused all payment for it; the professor ate like four men, Hans thanked the hosts with a single bow, Axel could not stop looking at the ordinary blue sky, and the two Sicilians crossed themselves, certain they were entertaining either saints or cargo dropped by God by mistake.
sentences.zh: 渔民们喂他们面包和酒，怎么也不肯收钱；教授吃得顶四个人，汉斯向主人家鞠了唯一的一个躬，阿克塞尔望着那片普普通通的蓝天，眼睛挪都挪不开；两个西西里人则在胸前连连画十字，认定自己招待的不是圣徒，就是上帝错手掉落的货物。

sentences.en: Hans took his wages with a small bow and turned north for Iceland without one word of farewell, as if the centre of the earth had been a job of work now finished; certain men, Axel wrote, are made of the same quiet as the subterranean world, and no summit ever thaws them.
sentences.zh: 汉斯领了工钱，微微一躬，转身北上回冰岛，没有一句道别，仿佛地心不过是一件做完了的活计；阿克塞尔写道：有些人生来就带着地下世界那种安静，登上任何山顶，也化不开他们。

sentences.en: Back in Hamburg, the professor gave his account before the scientific societies; the instruments were lost, the thermometer and all the rest now travelling somewhere inside the earth without them, so the story stood upon his word alone — and the societies, after a decent interval, elected him anyway, for fame, like steam, will rise through any old pipe.
sentences.zh: 回到汉堡，教授向各家科学学会讲述见闻；仪器都丢了，温度计和其余的家当如今正撇下他们，在大地深处某处独自旅行；这个故事便只立在他一个人的话上——而各家学会，在一段体面的观望之后，终究还是把他选了进去；可见名望这东西和蒸汽一样，再旧的管子也压不住它往上冒。

sentences.en: "We never reached the centre," he admitted freely; "the terrestrial furnace stopped us, as it stopped Saknussemm, and what we have instead is one new fact about the temperature of the deep — and a fact, gentlemen, is the only luggage a geologist brings back that the customs officers cannot tax."
sentences.zh: "我们没能到达地心，"他坦然承认，"地下的炉子挡住了我们，就像当年挡住萨克努姗一样；我们带回来的，是关于深处温度的一个新事实——而一个事实，诸位，是地质学家带回来的行李里唯一一样海关征不了税的东西。"

sentences.en: "Every instrument we carried down and every fact we carried up now belong to geology; the science of the earth has been carried three hundred feet into the earth itself, and that is a start which others, better provided, will finish."
sentences.zh: "我们带下去的每件仪器、带上来的每个事实，如今都归地质学所有；这门大地的科学，已经被送进了大地三百英尺——这是一个开头，会有准备更充分的人来把它完成。"

sentences.en: Gräuben married Axel in the spring, and the professor delivered the wedding breakfast a lecture on the thermal structure of the planet, which the guests survived; the happiest of men, Axel wrote in the last pages, is the one whose adventures are all behind him and whose science is all ahead.
sentences.zh: 开春，格劳本嫁给了阿克塞尔；婚宴上，教授就行星的热结构发表了一通讲话，宾客们总算挺了过来；阿克塞尔在最后几页里写道：最幸福的人，是冒险全都在身后、而科学全都在前头的那种人。

sentences.en: Axel submitted this diary to Gräuben and to the reader, ending with his uncle's own words: science is the courage to descend; and if the reader should ever come upon a parchment of runic letters in an old bookshop, let him remember that the terrain of the earth is not all above the waterline, and that the door of the cellar, in geology, is never locked.
sentences.zh: 阿克塞尔把这本日记交给格劳本，也交给读者，并用伯父自己的话收尾：科学，就是向下走的勇气；倘若读者哪天在旧书店里也碰到一页写着如尼字母的羊皮纸，请记住：大地的疆域并不全在水面之上；在地质学里，地窖的门，从来就没有锁过。

questions.q: What did the rusted dagger in the ash prove to Axel?
options: That treasure was buried further along the shore.
That Saknussemm had stood there and been stopped by the same wall.
That the dagger belonged to Hans's grandfather.
That natives were still living underground.
questions.explain: 第2句 "Saknussemm himself had stood here, stopped by the same stone"——三百年前的先行者同样被这面岩壁挡住，这柄薄了的刀刃是"过去签下的一份证人证词"。

questions.q: How did the party get past the granite wall?
options: They climbed over it at low tide.
Hans dug beneath it for a week.
The professor blasted it open with a gunpowder mine, and the sea poured in.
They turned back along the subterranean shore.
questions.explain: 第3句 "the professor constructed a mine of gunpowder... the blast opened the granite, and the sea poured in upon them, raft and all"——火药炸开岩壁，海水连人带筏灌入裂口。

questions.q: What carried the raft back up to the surface world?
options: A whale pushing from below.
Hans rowing without pause for three days.
The wind of the underground storm.
Steam in an old volcanic pipe — a geothermal lift going up.
questions.explain: 第5句教授喊出 "a geyser pipe, a geothermal lift, and it is going up"，第6句 "the old volcanic pipe had become a lift driven by geothermal fire"，蒸汽把他们托出火山口，抛进地中海。

questions.q: Hans left for Iceland without a word of farewell. What does this reveal about him?
options: He was angry at the professor's risky blast.
To Hans the whole journey was simply work, now finished — a quiet man's contract, not an adventure.
He could not speak any language but Icelandic.
He feared the people of Stromboli had cursed him.
questions.explain: 第9句 "as if the centre of the earth had been a job of work now finished"，阿克塞尔总结"有些人生来带着地下世界那种安静"——对汉斯而言，这是做完便结账的活计，而非需要告别的冒险。

questions.q: The sea they landed in is called the Mediterranean. With terr meaning land, what does the name say about this sea?
options: It is the warmest sea on earth.
It lies in the middle of the lands — surrounded by land on all sides.
It covers the centre of the terrestrial globe.
It was named by Saknussemm in his journal.
questions.explain: 第6句 "the warm sea of the Mediterranean"——medi（中间）+ terr（土地）+ anean，字面即"在诸陆中间"的海洋，斯特龙博利正位于被陆地环抱的地中海之中。
